title: ר' חייא בר פפא

paragraphs: R. Chiyya bar Pappa. Sanhedrin 34b: “Whence are these matters? R. Chiyya bar Pappa said.” Maharsha writes that it should read “Rav Acha bar Pappa.” Why he emends it this way requires investigation. Perhaps he thought this was one of Rav Pappa's eleven sons, among whom there was no son named R. Chiyya. But why did he not emend Bava Kamma 80b: “R. Abba bar Pappa, in the name of R. Chiyya bar Pappa, in the name of Acha bar Pappa”? Furthermore, R. Chiyya bar Pappa spoke in Acha bar Pappa's name. Also Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Keitzad Mevarkhin, has R. Chiyya bar Pappa before R. Zeira. It is difficult for there to be an error in three places.
